\pl{0.00}{(that is) Behold, the hope of fruit and of salvation shall be false to}
\pl{1.20}{itself for ever, unless thou rescue thy soul this very night.}
\pl{0.00}{And if such an examination be made for some days, or for one}
\pl{1.20}{month at the least (with repentance), it will suffice that}
\pl{1.20}{a perfect habit of virtue be bred.}
\parasep
\pl{4.80}{————————}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{\emph{There followeth the Morning Hymn, of most ancient use in the}}
\pl{0.00}{\emph{Church, out of the Alexandrine MS. of the King's Library.\hspace{0.60em}There}}
\pl{0.00}{\emph{is added the Evening Hymn also, because it is old.\hspace{0.60em}Concerning}}
\pl{0.00}{\emph{both, the Rev. Ussher is to be consulted, pp.} 41, 43, \emph{Book of the Creeds.}}
}

\sectionhead{§42 ΥΜΝΟΣ ΕΩΘΙΝΟΣ / *Hymnus Matutinus* + ΥΜΝΟΣ ΕΣΠΕΡΙΝΟΣ / *Hymnus Vespertinus*}

\pglabel{printed 388}{Greek}

\pl{3.60}{ΥΜΝΟΣ ΕΩΘΙΝΟΣ.*}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{ΔΟΞΑ ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ,}
\pl{1.20}{καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη,}
\pl{1.20}{ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία.}
\pl{0.00}{Αἰνοῦμέν σε,}
\pl{1.20}{εὐλογοῦμέν σε,}
\pl{1.20}{προσκυνοῦμέν σε,}
\pl{1.20}{δοξολογοῦμέν σε,}
\pl{1.20}{εὐχαριστοῦμέν σοι,}
\pl{1.20}{διὰ τὴν μεγάλην σου δόξαν,}
\pl{0.00}{Κύριε βασιλεῦ ἐπουράνιε,}
\pl{1.20}{Θεὲ Πατὲρ παντοκράτορ,}
\pl{1.20}{Κύριε Υἱὲ μονογενὲς,}
\pl{1.20}{Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ,}
\pl{1.20}{καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα.}
\pl{0.00}{Κύριε ὁ Θεὸς,}
\pl{1.20}{ὁ Ἀμνὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ,}
\pl{1.20}{ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Πατρὸς,}
\pl{0.00}{Ὁ αἴρων τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ κόσμου,}
\pl{1.20}{ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.}
\pl{0.00}{Ὁ αἴρων τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ κόσμου,}
\pl{1.20}{πρόσδεξαι τὴν δέησιν ἡμῶν.}
\pl{0.00}{Ὁ καθήμενος ἐν δεξιᾷ τοῦ Πατρὸς,}
\pl{1.20}{ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.}
\parasep
\pl{1.20}{* Hoc forsitan Carmen illud est, cujus meminit C. Plinius in Epistola}
\pl{0.00}{xxvii. lib. x. hisce verbis, "Quod essent soliti Christiani stato die ante lucem}
\pl{0.00}{convenire, Carmenque Christo quasi Deo dicere secum invicem."}

\pglabel{printed 388}{English}

{\itshape
\pl{3.60}{THE MORNING HYMN.*}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{GLORY be to God on high,}
\pl{1.20}{and on earth peace,}
\pl{1.20}{good will among men.}
\pl{0.00}{We praise thee,}
\pl{1.20}{we bless thee,}
\pl{1.20}{we worship thee,}
\pl{1.20}{we glorify thee,}
\pl{1.20}{we give thanks to thee,}
\pl{1.20}{for thy great glory,}
\pl{0.00}{O Lord, heavenly King,}
\pl{1.20}{O God the Father Almighty,}
\pl{1.20}{O Lord, the only-begotten Son,}
\pl{1.20}{Jesu Christ,}
\pl{1.20}{and O Holy Ghost.}
\pl{0.00}{O Lord God,}
\pl{1.20}{the Lamb of God,}
\pl{1.20}{the Son of the Father,}
\pl{0.00}{Thou that takest away the sins of the world,}
\pl{1.20}{have mercy upon us.}
\pl{0.00}{Thou that takest away the sins of the world,}
\pl{1.20}{receive our prayer.}
\pl{0.00}{Thou that sittest at the right hand of the Father,}
\pl{1.20}{have mercy upon us.}
\parasep
\pl{1.20}{* This is perhaps that Hymn which C. Pliny makes mention of, in the}
\pl{0.00}{Epistle xxvii. of book x., in these words: "That the Christians were wont on}
\pl{0.00}{a set day to meet before daylight, and to sing a Hymn to Christ as unto God,}
\pl{0.00}{by turns among themselves."}
}

\pglabel{printed 389}{Latin}

\pl{2.40}{HYMNUS MATUTINUS.}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{GLORIA in excelsis Deo,}
\pl{1.20}{et in terra pax,}
\pl{1.20}{in hominibus bonæ voluntates.}
\pl{0.00}{Laudamus Te,}
\pl{1.20}{benedicimus Te,}
\pl{1.20}{adoramus Te,}
\pl{1.20}{glorificamus Te,}
\pl{1.20}{gratias agimus Tibi,}
\pl{1.20}{propter magnam gloriam Tuam,}
\pl{0.00}{Domine Deus Rex cœlestis,}
\pl{1.20}{Deus Pater omnipotens,}
\pl{1.20}{Domine Fili unigenite,}
\pl{1.20}{Jesu Christe.}
\pl{2.40}{\emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ }}
\pl{0.00}{Domine Deus,}
\pl{1.20}{Agnus Dei,}
\pl{1.20}{Filius Patris,}
\pl{0.00}{Qui tollis peccata mundi,}
\pl{1.20}{miserere nobis.}
\pl{0.00}{Qui tollis peccata mundi,}
\pl{1.20}{suscipe deprecationem nostram.}
\pl{0.00}{Qui sedes ad dexteram Patris,}
\pl{1.20}{miserere nobis.}

\pglabel{printed 390}{Greek}

\pl{0.00}{Ὅτι σὺ εἶ μόνος ἅγιος,}
\pl{1.20}{σὺ εἶ μόνος κύριος,}
\pl{1.20}{Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς,}
\pl{2.40}{\emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ }}
\pl{0.00}{εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ Πατρός.\hspace{0.90em}Ἀμήν.}
\parasep
\pl{3.60}{————————}
\parasep
\pl{3.60}{ΥΜΝΟΣ ΕΣΠΕΡΙΝΟΣ.}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{ΦΩΣ ἱλαρὸν ἁγίας δόξης}
\pl{2.40}{ἀθανάτου Πατρὸς, οὐρανίου, ἁγίου,}
\pl{1.20}{μάκαρος, Ἰησοῦ Χριστὲ,}
\pl{0.00}{ἐλθόντες ἐπὶ τοῦ ἡλίου δύσιν,}
\pl{1.20}{ἰδόντες φῶς ἑσπερινὸν,}
\pl{2.40}{ὑμνοῦμεν Πατέρα,}
\pl{3.60}{καὶ Υἱὸν,}
\pl{2.40}{καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ.}
\pl{0.00}{Ἄξιος εἶ ἐν πᾶσι καιροῖς}
\pl{1.20}{ὑμνεῖσθαι φωναῖς ὁσίαις,}
\pl{2.40}{Υἱὲ Θεοῦ,}
\pl{3.60}{ζωὴν ὁ διδούς.}
\pl{0.00}{Διὸ ὁ κόσμος σε δοξάζει.}

\pglabel{printed 390}{English}

{\itshape
\pl{0.00}{For thou only art holy,}
\pl{1.20}{thou only art Lord,}
\pl{1.20}{Jesus Christ,}
\pl{2.40}{\emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ } \emph{ }}
\pl{0.00}{unto the glory of God the Father.\hspace{0.90em}Amen.}
\parasep
\pl{3.60}{————————}
\parasep
\pl{3.60}{THE EVENING HYMN.}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{O GLADSOME light of the holy glory}
\pl{2.40}{of the immortal Father, heavenly, holy,}
\pl{1.20}{blessed, O Jesu Christ,}
\pl{0.00}{we, being come to the setting of the sun,}
\pl{1.20}{beholding the evening light,}
\pl{2.40}{praise in hymns the Father,}
\pl{3.60}{and the Son,}
\pl{2.40}{and the Holy Spirit of God.}
\pl{0.00}{Worthy art thou at all times}
\pl{1.20}{to be hymned with holy voices,}
\pl{2.40}{O Son of God,}
\pl{3.60}{thou giver of life.}
\pl{0.00}{Wherefore the world doth glorify thee.}
}

\pglabel{printed 391}{Latin}

\pl{1.20}{Quoniam Tu solus sanctus,}
\pl{2.40}{Tu solus Dominus,}
\pl{2.40}{Jesu Christe,}
\pl{2.40}{cum Sancto Spiritu,}
\pl{2.40}{in gloria Dei Patris.\hspace{0.90em}Amen.}
\parasep
\pl{3.60}{————————}
\parasep
\pl{2.40}{HYMNUS VESPERTINUS.}
\parasep
\pl{0.00}{LUMEN hilare sanctæ gloriæ}
\pl{2.40}{Immortalis Patris, cœlestis,}
\pl{3.60}{sancti, beati, Jesu Christe;}
\pl{0.00}{quum ad solis occasum pervenerimus,}
\pl{1.20}{lumen cernentes vespertinum,}
\pl{2.40}{laudamus Patrem,}
\pl{3.60}{Filium,}
\pl{1.20}{et Sanctum Spiritum Dei.}
\pl{0.00}{Dignus es in tempore quovis}
\pl{1.20}{sanctis vocibus celebrari,}
\pl{2.40}{Fili Dei,}
\pl{3.60}{vitæ dator,}
\pl{0.00}{Quapropter Te mundus glorificat.}

\sectionhead{§43 ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΧΡΙΣΤΟΥ ΣΤΑΥΡΩΣΙΝ, Μονοστροφικά / *In Christum Crucifixum, Monostrophica*}

\pglabel{printed 392}{Greek}

\pl{2.40}{ΕΙΣ ΤΗΝ ΤΟΥ ΧΡΙΣΤΟΥ ΣΤΑΥΡΩΣΙΝ}
\pl{4.80}{Μονοστροφικά.}
\parasep
\pl{1.20}{Ἄλις ἐνθέου φλυάρου}
\pl{1.20}{Ἄμειβε, Μοῦσα, χορδὰς,}
\pl{1.20}{Καὶ βάρβιτον λαβοῦσα,}
\pl{1.20}{Σεμνὸν κρότησον ὕμνον}
\pl{1.20}{Σταυρουμένῳ Ἄνακτι.}
\pl{1.20}{Ὦ θαυμάτων ἄπληστε}
\pl{1.20}{Θησαυρὲ, κἀπέραντε·}
\pl{2.40}{Τί Σοι, τί πρῶτον εἴπω;}
\pl{0.00}{Θέλω λέγειν ἀνέκφατον βροτοῖσι,}
\pl{1.20}{Μακάρεσσί τε δαίμοσι γρῖφον,}
\pl{3.60}{Πᾶς, Θεὸς ὢν, ἔθανες!}
\pl{0.00}{Θέλω λέγειν ἀνιχνίαστα βένθη}
\pl{1.20}{Ἐλέου, ὅτι λύτρον ὑπ' ἐχθρῶν}
\pl{3.60}{Υἱὸν ἔδωκε Πατήρ.}
\pl{3.60}{Θέλω ὑψόθ' ἀῦσαι}
\pl{3.60}{Θέσφατον θρίαμβον}
\pl{3.60}{Τριημέροιο νεκροῦ,}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ αἰχμάλωτον Ἅιδην,}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ θάνατον θανάτῳ δαμέντα.}
\pl{0.00}{Ἀλλά μοι ἀμφιβρέμει Κρανίων ὄρος,}
\pl{0.00}{Καὶ πολύθρου κελάδου γέμει οὔατα,}
\pl{3.60}{ὀλλύντων, ὀλλυμένων τε.}
\pl{1.20}{Ἐκθόρετ' ἐς λόφον ὄμματα,}
\pl{1.20}{Τίς μέσσος κρέμαται τριῶν,}
\pl{1.20}{(Ὡς οὐδὲν δυσὶν ἴκελος,)}

\pglabel{printed 392}{English}

{\itshape
\pl{2.40}{ON THE CRUCIFYING OF CHRIST}
\pl{4.80}{Monostrophics.}
\parasep
\pl{1.20}{ENOUGH of inspired babbling;}
\pl{1.20}{Change, O Muse, thy strings,}
\pl{1.20}{and taking up the lyre,}
\pl{1.20}{strike a solemn hymn}
\pl{1.20}{to the King upon his cross.}
\pl{1.20}{O Treasure of wonders, unsated}
\pl{1.20}{and unbounded:}
\pl{2.40}{What shall I say to thee, and what first?}
\pl{0.00}{I would tell a thing unspeakable to mortals,}
\pl{1.20}{and a riddle to the blessed spirits,}
\pl{3.60}{How, being God, thou didst die!}
\pl{0.00}{I would tell the untrackable deeps}
\pl{1.20}{of Mercy, that for a ransom, at the hands of enemies,}
\pl{3.60}{the Father gave the Son.}
\pl{3.60}{I would cry aloud on high}
\pl{3.60}{the oracled triumph}
\pl{3.60}{of the three-days' dead,}
\pl{3.60}{and Hades led captive,}
\pl{3.60}{and death subdued by death.}
\pl{0.00}{But the hill of Skulls roars round about me,}
\pl{0.00}{and mine ears are full of a many-voiced clamour,}
\pl{3.60}{of them that destroy, and them that perish.}
\pl{1.20}{Leap forth to the hill, mine eyes;}
\pl{1.20}{who is it hangeth in the midst of three,}
\pl{1.20}{(how nothing like unto the two!)}
}

\pglabel{printed 393}{Latin}

\pl{2.40}{IN CHRISTUM CRUCIFIXUM}
\pl{4.80}{MONOSTROPHICA.}
\parasep
\pl{1.20}{SATIS fuit inspirationis nugatoriæ;}
\pl{1.20}{Musa, permuta chordas,}
\pl{1.20}{Et, barbito arrepto,}
\pl{1.20}{Augustum insona hymnum}
\pl{1.20}{Crucifixo Regi.}
\pl{1.20}{O miraculorum vaste}
\pl{1.20}{Thesaure, atque immense!}
\pl{2.40}{Quid tuum, quid primum dixero?}
\pl{0.00}{Vellem dicere inenarrabile hominibus}
\pl{1.20}{Beatisque Angelis ænigma,}
\pl{3.60}{Qui, Deus immortalis, mortuus es?}
\pl{0.00}{Vellem dicere imperscrutandas profunditates}
\pl{1.20}{Misericordiæ, quia lytrum pro hostibus}
\pl{3.60}{Filium præbuit Pater.}
\pl{3.60}{Vellem sublimiter eloqui}
\pl{3.60}{Mysticum triumphum}
\pl{3.60}{Triduani cadaveris,}
\pl{3.60}{Et captivum orcum,}
\pl{3.60}{Mortemque morte profligatam.}
\pl{0.00}{Nisi quod mihi circumfremit Calvariorum mons,}
\pl{0.00}{Et fragoso strepitu gravantur aures}
\pl{3.60}{Perdentium, pereuntiumque.}
\pl{1.20}{Exsilite ad collem, oculi;}
\pl{1.20}{Quis medius trium pendet,}
\pl{1.20}{(Quam nil duobus ille similis!)}

\pglabel{printed 394}{Greek}

\pl{1.20}{Ἐκ δ' ἐτάθη τετράζυγι πρέμνῳ;}
\pl{3.60}{Πρῆϋ κάρηνον}
\pl{3.60}{Ἡδέως κεκυφὼς,}
\pl{0.00}{Καὶ ὠλενῶν ἱερὸν κράτος}
\pl{0.00}{Ἐγκάρσιον πετάσσας,}
\pl{4.80}{Νηλεέσσι γόμφοις}
\pl{0.00}{Πεπαρμένον ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα!}
\pl{0.00}{Ἄνθρωπε τάλαν, ταῦτ' ἀπαθὴς βλέπεις;}
\pl{3.60}{Οἴμωζε πολλὰ,}
\pl{3.60}{Ἐσθῆτα ῥῆξον,}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ τύπτε στέρνον,}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ τίλλε χαίτην,}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ σπλάγχνα κινοῦ·}
\pl{0.00}{Ἡ οὐχ ὁράας ὁλοπόρφυρον;}
\pl{3.60}{Στίλβοντ' οὐ φλογὶ}
\pl{3.60}{Σιδονίης ἁλὸς, ἀλ-}
\pl{1.20}{λ' αἵματι σταζομένῳ,}
\pl{3.60}{Τῷ μὲν ἀπὸ κροτάφων}
\pl{3.60}{Κυκλουμένων ἀκάνθης}
\pl{3.60}{Ὀξυστόμοισι κουραῖς·}
\pl{3.60}{Τῷ δὲ καὶ ἐκ μελέων}
\pl{3.60}{Κεχαραγμένων ἱμάσθλης}
\pl{3.60}{Πικρῇσι συμπλοκῇσι.}
\pl{3.60}{Ἄνοιγ', ἄνοιγε}
\pl{3.60}{Πύλας ὀπωπῶν}
\pl{3.60}{Καὶ πηγὰς βλεφάρων}
\pl{0.00}{Λῦσαι·\hspace{0.90em}Ψέκαζε, δεῦε γαῖαν,}
\pl{3.60}{Σὺν τῷ ἀφειδῶς}
\pl{3.60}{Ἑὸν αἷμα χέαν-}
\pl{1.20}{τ'. ὀλίγ' ἄττα λείβειν δάκρυα}
\pl{3.60}{Τίς φθόνος, ὦ βροτέ;}

\pglabel{printed 394}{English}

{\itshape
\pl{1.20}{and is stretched out upon the four-yoked stock?}
\pl{3.60}{his gentle head}
\pl{3.60}{sweetly bowed down,}
\pl{0.00}{and the holy strength of his arms}
\pl{0.00}{spread abroad athwart,}
\pl{4.80}{with pitiless nails}
\pl{0.00}{pierced through on this side and on that!}
\pl{0.00}{Wretched man, dost thou look on this unmoved?}
\pl{3.60}{Wail sore,}
\pl{3.60}{rend thy garment,}
\pl{3.60}{and smite thy breast,}
\pl{3.60}{and tear thy hair,}
\pl{3.60}{and stir thy bowels.}
\pl{0.00}{Dost thou not see him all in purple?}
\pl{3.60}{gleaming not with the flame}
\pl{3.60}{of the Sidonian sea, but}
\pl{1.20}{with blood dripping down,}
\pl{3.60}{the one part from his temples}
\pl{3.60}{girt about with the thorn's}
\pl{3.60}{sharp-mouthed shearing;}
\pl{3.60}{the other from his limbs}
\pl{3.60}{scored with the scourge's}
\pl{3.60}{bitter embracings.}
\pl{3.60}{Open, open}
\pl{3.60}{the gates of thine eyes,}
\pl{3.60}{and the springs of thine eyelids}
\pl{0.00}{loose:\hspace{0.90em}drizzle down, wet the earth,}
\pl{3.60}{with him that unsparingly}
\pl{3.60}{poureth out his own blood.}
\pl{1.20}{To shed some few tears —}
\pl{3.60}{what grudging is that, O mortal?}
}

\pglabel{printed 395}{Latin}

\pl{1.20}{Extensus quadrijugo stipite?}
\pl{3.60}{Mansuetum caput}
\pl{3.60}{Amœne inclinans,}
\pl{0.00}{Et brachiorum sacrum robur}
\pl{0.00}{Transversum expandens,}
\pl{4.80}{Immitibus clavis}
\pl{0.00}{Perfossum hic et illic.}
\pl{0.00}{Homo miselle, hæccine immotus aspicis?}
\pl{3.60}{Plora ubertim,}
\pl{3.60}{Vestem conscinde,}
\pl{3.60}{Et tunde pectus,}
\pl{3.60}{Ac vellica crinem,}
\pl{3.60}{Medullitusque perturbare.}
\pl{0.00}{Nonne cernis totum-purpuratum?}
\pl{3.60}{Sed haud fulgentem flamma}
\pl{3.60}{Tyrii maris, verum}
\pl{3.60}{Sanguine stillante,}
\pl{3.60}{Partim a temporibus}
\pl{3.60}{Cinctis spinarum}
\pl{3.60}{Acriter mordente incisura;}
\pl{3.60}{Partim ex artubus}
\pl{3.60}{Insignitis flagellis}
\pl{3.60}{Amaro amplexu.}
\pl{3.60}{Aperi, aperi}
\pl{3.60}{Portas oculorum;}
\pl{3.60}{Et fontes palpebrarum}
\pl{0.00}{Solve:\hspace{0.90em}irrora, madefac terram,}
\pl{3.60}{Cum illo largiter}
\pl{3.60}{Proprium cruorem effundente.}
\pl{0.00}{Pauculas quasdam distillare lachrymas}
\pl{3.60}{Quænam invidia sit, O homo?}
